newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total denies gas deal with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Total denies gas deal with Iran.

text.p: French oil company Total SA denied on Sunday it had signed a contract with Iran to develop its major South Pars gas field, but said it was interested in the project and talks were still going on.

"No contract has been signed between Total and Iran for the development of South Pars, but the project does interest us," a spokesman said after reports of a deal worth $3.5 billion. "The negotiations are continuing," the spokesman said.

Iran's Foreign Affairs Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said in Tehran on Sunday that Iran had awarded Total the contract, which oil experts say would require the single biggest investment in the Islamic Republic since its 1979 revolution.

Velayati said the deal with Total, and the interest of European and American firms in an energy conference in the Iranian city of Isfahan earlier this month, showed sanctions by the United States were having no impact on Iran.
But an official at Iran's state oil company said talks were still continuing with Total and also with a rival consortium led by the Anglo-Dutch oil giant Royal Dutch Shell.

Total and Shell have led groups of European and Asian firms aiming to develop South Pars to produce 56.64 million cubic metres a day of gas after five years of project work. Total is already the leading foreign oil investor in Iran after scooping a $600 million deal in 1995 to develop its Sirri E and A offshore gas fields, the latter of which starts production next year.
